question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP
request.body: A single GET of the Help Center article search endpoint on support.optimizely.com, query 'billing', per_page 3. No credential, no cookie jar, no custom User-Agent. A second request in the same transcript searched 'plan options and costs'.

decoded.result: count 164 for the query 'billing', three results returned, each with title, html_url and the article's full body HTML, including "Manage your account's plan and invoices" and "Usage and billing dashboards"
decoded.why-it-matters-here: both product surfaces this entry measures, the MCP server and the REST API, refuse a stranger with 401; this support-search surface is the one measured route by which an agent with no Optimizely account reaches the vendor's own account-administration documentation, and it is how the billing evidence in version 4 of this entry was located
decoded.second-instance: the same endpoint answered the same way on support.zendesk.com the same day; that measurement is proposed as p-20260924-zendesk-keyless-hc-search in PR #155 and was not on main when this record was filed, so it is pending evidence, not a filed record, and nothing here depends on it
decoded.not-measured: anything behind an Optimizely credential; whether an instance can turn this off; whether the rate limit is per IP or per instance
decoded.user-agent: the published command sends curl's default User-Agent; the 12:28Z request sent an unrecorded one, and the 18:04Z re-run with the default (section 5 of the artifact) answered the same status, count and rate-limit headers, so the observation does not depend on it
decoded.correction: version 1 of this record said x-rate-limit 10000; the artifact's section 1 says 700 and always did (the 10000 was copied from the Zendesk record); corrected 2026-09-24 on PR #156 before merge
decoded.usage-articles: sections 6 to 8 of the artifact (appended 2026-09-25, after the reviewer's second change request) locate the three usage articles the profile names ('Review impression usage', 'Monitor monthly active users (MAUs)', 'Troubleshoot MAU overages') through the same keyless search, list the 'Account administration' section that holds them beside the two billing articles, and read all three whole: none states a figure per impression, per MAU or per overage

finding: An agent with no Optimizely account, no key and no cookie can search Optimizely's support help centre through the Zendesk REST API it runs on and receive whole articles: 164 matches for 'billing', including the vendor's own account-administration pages. It changes nothing about access to the product: both product surfaces this entry measures, the MCP server and the REST API, answer 401. It is a documented anonymous permission of the help-centre software rather than a lapse. What it establishes is that for a vendor whose measured product surfaces refuse a stranger, the documentation of how that vendor bills is machine-readable to one.
